bottom_line: AI and tech stocks crashed this week. It was tech's worst week on Wall Street since 2020, and the S&P 500 and the Dow fell into a 'correction', meaning a 10% drop from their high. On top of that, the Fed (the people who set interest rates) looks set to RAISE rates next month because prices are still rising too fast.

stories.title: The AI stock boom cracked
stories.real: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Nasdaq is now negative for the year. Chip stocks had their worst week since 2001, and Nvidia fell 14%, its longest weekly losing streak since 2008. Nvidia dropped from the most valuable company in the world to fourth, behind Apple, Microsoft and Alphabet. Anthropic's record stock-market debut ran straight into the sell-off, and its shares slid. AI stocks drove this year's big gains, so when they fall, the whole market falls with them.

stories.title: The Fed is likely to raise rates
stories.real: Notes from the Fed's last meeting say higher interest rates are needed in December because worries about inflation (prices rising) keep growing. Fed officials Christopher Waller and Lisa Cook point the same way, and Cook warned of larger hikes. The open question isn't whether they raise, but by how much.
stories.you: Higher rates mean credit cards, car loans and mortgages get more expensive to borrow on, while savings accounts can pay a bit more.

stories.title: Trump keeps hammering the Fed
stories.real: Trump again says interest rates are too high and that the Fed has become 'politicized'. He points to India's 7% growth and claims the US could grow far faster with lower rates. The Fed is still heading the other way.
stories.you: A public fight between the President and the Fed adds uncertainty, but the Fed, not the President, sets rates.

stories.title: A 10% cap on credit card interest
stories.real: Trump says he'll work with Democrats to cap credit card interest rates at 10%. It's a promise to work on it, not a law yet.
stories.you: If it ever passes, people who carry a card balance would pay a lot less interest, but nothing has changed on your bill today.
